subject: bowhead whale
title: The 5 Heaviest Whales, Ranked (Most People Never Heard of #2)

scenes.text: The five heaviest whales. Most people have never heard of number two.
Number five: the sperm whale. Big males reach about forty-five tons, just beating the humpback.
scenes.label: Sperm whale · 45 tons

scenes.text: Number four: the fin whale. Up to eighty tons, and the second-longest whale alive.
scenes.label: Fin whale · 80 tons

scenes.text: Number three: the North Pacific right whale. Up to a hundred tons, and one of the rarest whales on Earth.
scenes.label: N. Pacific right · 100 tons

scenes.text: Number two: the bowhead. A hundred tons or more, with a skull that punches through Arctic ice.
scenes.label: Bowhead · 100+ tons

scenes.text: Number one: the blue whale. Up to about a hundred and sixty-five tons, over sixty tons more than the bowhead.
scenes.label: Blue whale · 165 tons

description:
The second-heaviest whale on Earth is one most people have never heard of: the Arctic bowhead.
NOAA Fisheries lists bowheads and North Pacific right whales at up to about 100 tons, fin whales at up to 80, and big male sperm whales at about 45. The blue whale tops them all at up to about 330,000 pounds.
Which whale did you expect at number two?
first_comment: Bowheads may also live 200 years or more. Which whale would you have put at number one, and what should we rank next?
